newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Dec 20.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Dec 20.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

At the Australian short-course swimming championships in Melbourne yesterday, 19-year-old Michael Klim twice bettered a national 200m freestyle record that had stood for nine years and set the fastest time in the world this year for the 100m butterfly. Pge 20.

The West Indies showed none of their match-winning form against Pakistan yesterday, when they allowed Victoria to bolt to 354 on the first day of their four-day match at Wangaratta. Victorian Graeme Vimpani scored his maiden first-class century, before bing stumped at 133. Page 20.

Tasmanian Shaun Young took 7-64 yesterday as Pakistan were dismissed for 299 on day one of the four-day match at Hobart's Bellrive Oval. Young's bowling performance, teamed with successive Sheffield Shield centuries, make him one of the best performing cicket all-rounders this season. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Although the Australian women's hockey team had its 41-Test unbeaten streak ruined on Wednesday, when India upset a rejigged Australian team 3-0 in Delhi, the Hockeyroos have established themselves as one of Australia's pre-eminent sporting teams of all tme, beating 12 nations, including the rest of the world's top eight, two major tournaments and the gold medal at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics. Page 48.

Wollongong will be the only bid city to miss out on hosting soccer games for the 2000 Olympics, after Sydney's Homebush Stadium, Melbourne, Brisbane, Canberra and Adelaide were named as the venues for Olympic soccer. FIFA has requested the opening match e played in the Olympic Stadium, with Australia almost certain to feature. Page 48.

Sydney Swans full-forward Tony Lockett will attend an interview with Victorian Police in relation to an investigation which began 12 months ago into the alleged substitution of greyhound sires for breeding purposes. One man was charged yesterday with 28 counts of forgery and deception, but there is no suggestion that Lockett is facing charges. Page 48.
THE AGE

Following an incident between Carlton's Matthew Hogg and Mick McGuane at training on Wednesday - McGuane was intoxicated - the AFL will consider introducing drug and alcohol testing at early-morning training sessions. However, at this stage, the Australin Sports Drug Agency is permitted only to take urine samples of footballers. Page C8.

Hawthorn half-forward Paul Hudson will continue his career with the Western Bulldogs next year, prompting anger from the Hawks who expressed disappointment at the timing of losing a quality player. Footscray is expected to announce today that Hudson has been guaranteed to be drafted by the Bulldogs in February. Page C8.

Four tennis officials stormed off court at Melbourne Park yesterday after former Wimbledon champion Pat Cash argued with the chair umpire and twice tossed his racquet away. Cash was trailing Grant Doyle 5-2 in the first set of their match at the Aussie Asault, but the players were forced to keep score for themselves. Page C8.
THE HERALD SUN

After being named as one of the host cities for Olympic soccer in 2000, Melbourne's new Docklands Stadium is almost certain to host the group in which Australia is drawn as Sydney will only host the opening games and a number of finals. Page 118.

Queensland bowler Andrew Bichel took a career-best 6-56 at the Gabba yesterday, as the Bulls dismissed New South Wales for 190 on the opening day of the Sheffield Shield cricket clash. Queensland was 2-89 at stumps, with Steve Waugh the only New South Waes batsman to make a stand on 55. Page 116.

Australian driver Craig Lowndes has signed to race for the champion RSM Marko team from Austria in 1997. Lowndes has been signed to a 10-year management contract by Scotsman Tom Walkinshaw, who owns the Holden Racing Team and the Arrows Formula One team. Page 112.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Former Australian cricket captain Allan Border has warned current captain Mark Taylor of the dangers of being overburdened as Test captain, claiming that he handed over much of the responsibility to coach Bob Simpson. However, Border has applauded Taylor for taking on so much responsibility and wishes that he had taken a more forceful role in his later years in the job. Page 96.

The Sydney Blues, on a league-best eight-game winning streak, will play the Melbourne Monarchs eight times in a row over the next two weekends, starting with the first half of a four-game series in Melbourne tonight, in a bid to defend their Australian Baeball League championship. Page 91.

Former world squash champion Australian Michelle Martin warned yesterday that she was determined to win back her world number one ranking from Victorian Sarah FitzGerald, who won the world championships in Kuala Lumpur this year. Page 90.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
